newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC divided on admitting new members, Manila says.
newsitem.headline: APEC divided on admitting new members, Manila says.

text.p: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum members are divided over whether to admit new members, a Philippine official said on Thursday.

"My sense is that APEC is divided down the line," Assistant Trade Secretary Edsel Custodio told reporters at a news briefing ahead of a meeting of APEC leaders where the issue is likely to be discussed.
Heads of state and government of APEC's 18 members hold their annual summit in Subic Bay in the Philippines on November 25.
The Philippines is chairing APEC this year and Custodio is head of the Philippine delegation to a senior officials meeting to be held five days before the summit.
The senior officials are expected to make a recommendation on the membership issue.
Russia, India, Vietnam, Peru and Mongolia are among 10 countries that have applied to join APEC which aims to free trade and investments within the region.
A three-year moratorium on accepting new members ends on November 25.
Custodio said unless all members agreed either to scrap or extend the moratorium, the moratorium would stay indefinitely.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore, South Korea and the United States.
